- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–15% in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., dropping from 45+ to 35–40), model overreacts; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model delays correction; anticipate a 2–3 day lag in price recovery; forecast should rise gradually.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 14-day average, flag as overconfident; reduce by 5–10% unless accompanied by strong bullish sentiment.
- In absence of clear event context, assume neutral sentiment; model should not overreact to minor price fluctuations; use 30-day smoothed average as baseline.
